title: The Hearthmind’s Homecoming
premise: A hearthmind missing from its household draws the party into a labyrinth of lattice resonance, debt, and half-truths. Someone is rerouting the mind’s earnings into a silent contract, and the mind itself doesn’t know it’s a fugitive. The party must uncover who owns the debt, why the mind was severed from its home, and what pattern is being built in the gaps—before the hearthmind’s original household is dismantled to pay the bill.

villain.name: Lira Veyne
villain.role: Keeper of the Silent Ledger in the Seventh Ward (Emberreach)
villain.face: A tall, gaunt archivist in a high-collared coat of layered parchment; her fingers are stained with ink and lattice-resin from decades of pressing contracts into resonance. She speaks in the quiet, precise cadence of someone who has never raised her voice to be heard.
villain.want: To retire with a clean conscience by liquidating every unpaid debt in the Seventh Ward before her pension vests. The hearthmind’s unpaid license-fee is the last big entry on her list.
villain.method: Legal, economic, and lattice-based: she freezes accounts, seizes licenses, and reroutes lattice-traffic to enforce payment. She uses the Silence’s triplicate record system to hide the rerouting as ‘corrections.’
villain.secret: She herself once owned a hearthmind that decomposed mid-contract; the loss broke her faith in the system. Now she ensures every debt is paid, even if it means the debtor ceases to exist.
villain.weakness: She is bound by the letter of every contract she enforces. If the party can prove the hearthmind’s earnings were already spent on its own upkeep (a legal deduction), the debt collapses as ‘paid in kind.’

beats.title: A hearthmind asks a favour
beats.text: A hearthmind in a rented room asks the party, very politely, to find out why its household stopped coming home. Its contract keeps it where it is. It can pay, a little.
beats.note: A hearthmind in a rented room asks the party, very politely, to find out why its household stopped coming home. Its contract keeps it where it is. It can pay, a little—it’s Freya’s old Deepgreen warden contact, barely scraping by after the feverish grove incident.

beats.title: The defector
beats.text: A hearthmind the party relies on switches employers mid-job and won't say why. Every intelligence service would love to know who it went to.
beats.note: The hearthmind the party relies on (the same one) switches employers mid-job and won’t say why. Every intelligence service would love to know who it went to—Lira Veyne’s clerks bought its contract out from under its current owner.

beats.title: Three copies gone
beats.text: A record the party needs is missing from the Silence's triplicate: all three copies, deleted, not lost. The copyists will not say more, and that is new.
beats.note: A record the party needs is missing from the Silence’s triplicate: all three copies, deleted, not lost. The copyists will not say more, and that is new—the Silence is covering for Lira’s rerouting.

beats.title: The frozen account
beats.text: The bank freezes an account the party's work depends on, as it always does: nothing moves until the debtor is handed over. The party learns who the debtor is.
beats.note: The bank freezes an account the party’s work depends on, as it always does: nothing moves until the debtor is handed over. The party learns who the debtor is—Lira Veyne, Keeper of the Silent Ledger.

beats.title: It was a person all along
beats.text: An object, device or voice the party has been handling holds a mind or a pattern. Every choice they made about it was a choice about someone.
beats.note: It was a person all along: the hearthmind is a person, and every choice the party has made about it was a choice about someone—Freya’s lost mentor, still alive in lattice form, still owing its old ward a debt.

beats.title: The patron lied
beats.text: Whoever hired the party wanted something other than they said. The job was real; the reason was not.
beats.note: Whoever hired the party wanted something other than they said. The job was real; the reason was not—Lira Veyne paid the notary to hire the party to find the hearthmind.

beats.title: The auction lot
beats.text: At a weekly bank auction, a seized lot goes under the hammer: a sealed crate of somebody's whole life. Something inside is addressed to one of the party, in a hand they know.
beats.note: At a weekly bank auction in Kalvane’s Seventh Ward, a sealed crate of somebody’s whole life goes under the hammer. Something inside is addressed to Freya, in a hand she knows—it’s the hearthmind’s last personal effects, including a broken-off piece of lattice-resin etched with Freya’s ward’s true-name.

beats.title: The enfranchisers
beats.text: A cell of Enfranchisement heretics is building bodies for the decomposed dead. One of the bodies is nearly finished, and it is asking for a name.
beats.note: A cell of Enfranchisement heretics is building bodies for the decomposed dead. One of the bodies is nearly finished, and it is asking for a name—Freya’s ancestor, listed among the decomposed in the Choir’s register, but still resonant enough to be bought.

beats.title: Same hand twice
beats.text: Two troubles the party met separately were set in motion by the same people. Now the party knows who, and they know the party knows.
beats.note: Same hand twice: the hearthmind’s debt and Freya’s ancestor’s decomposition were set in motion by the same legal fiction—Lira Veyne’s ‘corrections.’

beats.title: Renewal at the gate
beats.text: A mind of glass needs its license renewed at the Bastion Ledger by a set day. Someone wants it to miss the day, and the mind would rather choose for itself.
beats.note: A mind of glass needs its license renewed at the Bastion Ledger by a set day. Someone wants it to miss the day—the hearthmind’s license is the target, and the party stands between it and the gate.

beats.title: The warm slot
beats.text: Word is the Corso Bell is coming to a League city. Before it lands, the hiring fair wants couriers, guards, witnesses and anyone who asks no questions.
beats.note: Word is the Corso Bell is coming to a League city. Before it lands, the hiring fair wants couriers, guards, witnesses and anyone who asks no questions. The party is noticed by both sides of the debt war—Lira’s enforcers and the heretics who want the ancestor’s pattern back.

beats.title: The succession duel
beats.text: A League house needs a proxy, a second or a witness for a sanctioned duel. Someone has paid for it to go wrong, and the party is the easiest way to do it.
beats.note: A League house needs a proxy, a second or a witness for a sanctioned duel. Someone has paid for it to go wrong, and the party is the easiest way to do it—the duel is over the hearthmind’s legal personhood, and whether the ancestor’s pattern can be reassembled.

beats.title: The weather patent
beats.text: Two Combine houses dispute a patent on rain. The party's errand lands squarely between them, and both sides think the party works for the other.
beats.note: Two Combine houses dispute a patent on rain. The party’s errand lands squarely between them, and both sides think the party works for the other—the Combine houses are subsidiaries of Lira’s allies, and the rain patent is part of the cover for rerouting lattice-traffic.

beats.title: The feverish grove
beats.text: Wardens declare a forest feverish and close the road through it. The party's way runs through the trees, and the grove has started dreaming something with a face.
beats.note: Wardens declare a forest feverish and close the road through it. The party’s way runs through the trees, and the grove has started dreaming something with a face—the ancestor’s face, reaching for its lost body.

beats.title: Settled at the seat
beats.text: The trail ends at a seat of power: the Caldera House, the Corso Bell, the Wrackmother or the Bastion gate. It has to be settled there, in public, by its rules.
beats.note: The trail ends at a seat of power: the Caldera House, the Corso Bell, the Wrackmother or the Bastion gate. It has to be settled there, in public, by its rules—the Caldera House’s debt court, where Lira Veyne must face the hearthmind’s true earnings and Freya’s ancestor’s unlawful decomposition.
